page: Vultr voc-s-4c-32gb-960s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute server powered by an AMD EPYC processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core, running at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The processor includes 32 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache, supporting instruction sets such as AVX, AVX512F, AVX512_VNNI, AVX512_BF16, and AES. The system is equipped with 32.0 GB of RAM, providing 8.0 GB of memory per core, alongside 960 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and 1 complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU is included on this instance type.

Benchmark data reveals top-tier single-core CPU performance in stress-ng tests, alongside strong single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression. Large block memory write bandwidth and PassMark memory scores also rank in the top 25%. However, multi-threaded performance is more moderate, with stress-ng multi-core CPU performance, Geekbench multi-core scores, and software compilation tests falling in the average range. Tradeoffs are evident in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, static web serving throughput, and database operations, which all score in the bottom 25%. Large model LLM inference is also a bottleneck, with prompt processing for a 7B model ranking in the bottom 10%.

From a resource density perspective, this server offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 1:8, making it a qualitatively cost-efficient option for memory-intensive workloads that do not require massive parallel compute. The inclusion of a 960 GB NVMe SSD provides substantial local storage capacity. Given the strong single-core performance and memory capacity, this configuration is appropriate for memory-optimized applications, single-threaded processing tasks, caching layers, and general-purpose workloads with moderate concurrency requirements. It is less optimal for highly parallelized decompression, high-throughput web serving, or intensive database operations.
